idiom_name: typing.Protocol (or abc.ABC) implementor injected into a composing class
implementation_notes: The implementor is a typing.Protocol (structural subtyping, PEP 544) or an abc.ABC with @abstractmethod, and the abstraction is an ordinary class that stores it and forwards the primitives; nothing has to be declared for an object to be a valid implementor, which is why duck typing plus composition replaces the classic inherited structure in most code. Protocol is the modern default because it needs no inheritance and describes exactly the primitive methods the abstraction calls, while ABC remains the right choice when you need isinstance/issubclass checks, virtual subclass registration via ABCMeta.register, or shared helper behaviour on the base. Where the primitive set is a single callable, a plain function argument is an even simpler implementor; keep a protocol only when it documents a contract callers must satisfy.
code_sketch:
from typing import Protocol

class Renderer(Protocol):                    # Implementor: structural, no base class
    def circle(self, r: float) -> None: ...

class CircleShape:                           # Abstraction: composed, not inherited
    def __init__(self, renderer: Renderer, radius: float) -> None:
        self._renderer = renderer
        self._radius = radius

    def draw(self) -> None:
        self._renderer.circle(self._radius)
pitfalls: Protocol is erased at runtime: a class can satisfy it without importing it, and a renamed primitive fails only when the call happens - keep a @runtime_checkable gate plus a test that exercises the primitive set.
@runtime_checkable protocols with non-method members raise TypeError on isinstance, so an attribute-based implementor cannot be checked at runtime even though the decorator suggests otherwise.

ABCs need subclassing or explicit registration, so a third-party object cannot be an implementor without ABCMeta.register, whereas a Protocol accepts it structurally - picking the wrong one changes who may implement the primitive set.
